events.title: Flash 4 ships with a real scripting language
events.summary: Macromedia Flash 4 added variables, loops, and conditions — the precursor to ActionScript.
events.about: Flash filled browsers with animated, interactive content before HTML5 — cartoon intros, simple games, product demos, and clickable banners. Flash 4 added real scripting (if/else, variables) so designers could build menus and quizzes, not just timeline animations.

narrative.whyChosen: Flash turned the web from static pages into animated, interactive experiences before HTML5.
narrative.whyImportant: Developers could build games and apps in the browser without a full plugin stack beyond Flash.
narrative.problemSolved: Earlier Flash versions only supported simple timeline actions, not real programmatic control.

events.title: Apache Tomcat released
events.summary: Sun donated Tomcat to the Apache Software Foundation in June 1999 — the first open-source Java servlet container as Apache Tomcat 3.0.
events.about: Tomcat runs Java servlets and JSPs — the reference implementation James Duncan Davidson built at Sun before open-sourcing it at JavaOne. It powered early enterprise Java, JSP websites, and the Jakarta ecosystem. Ant was born as Tomcat's build tool. Example: deploy a `.war` file and Tomcat serves your servlet at `http://localhost:8080/myapp`.

narrative.whyChosen: Tomcat made Java servlet hosting open source and embeddable outside proprietary app servers.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the default servlet container and launched the Apache Jakarta/Java open-source wave.
narrative.problemSolved: Java web developers needed a free, portable runtime for servlets without buying WebLogic or WebSphere.
